summary: Er. Jon Polisle strongly opposes ORV use on public lands, calling for a complete ban on ATVs, snowmobiles, and all off-road vehicles from all public lands. He argues that their trail use causes erosion and unnecessary noise, and that private enterprise—not public lands—should provide areas for such recreation. He uses the analogy of a recreational caterpillar tractor to underscore the absurdity of allowing ORVs in natural settings.

statement.text:
2040 Wilson, Apt. 28 St. Paul, Minn. 55119 July 14, 1972
Director
Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
Department of the Interior
Washington, D.C. 20240
Subject: Statement Number INT - DES - 72 - 62
Dear Sir:
Concerning your Draft Environmental Statement, I ask that ATV, snowmobiles, and off the road vehicles in general be banned from use on all public lands. Their trail use, causing erosion and unnecessary noise should not be permitted.
If I bought a caterpillar tractor for recreation and asked to use it in a national forest I would be laughed at, so why should someone (and others will quickly follow) trail ride through the serene setting nature can provide.
Private enterprise supplies the equipment and private enterprise can supply the riding area for off the road vehicle; They should not be permitted on public lands.
Sincerely,
Er. Jon Polisle
